text:
Eva Chen: ran an nsys capture on the 4xA100 pool last night after the KV-cache perf alert. attaching the quick summary below, pls skim.

Raj Patel: thanks — saw the alert. is this the cold-warm transition you mentioned?

Eva Chen: yeah, spike happens when we switch from cold to warm for long seq requests. tail latency jumps ~2.1x for 99p.

perf-bot: nsys profile uploaded: s3://redwood/profiles/1905/kv-warm-sync.out.nsys :thumbsup:

Marta López: pasted top kernels from nsys --trace=nvtx report (total GPU time):
- fused_gemm_attention_v2            39.8%
- cublasGemmEx                         21.2%
- softmax_cuda                         7.4%
- attention_kv_cache_lookup            6.9%
- kv_cache_prefetch_worker             5.6%
- kv_rotate_and_concat                 4.1%
- memcpy_HtoD                          3.0%
- decode_token_kernel                  2.0%

Jin Park: wow fused_gemm_attention_v2 dominating. occupancy reports low SM util on that kernel — lots of small launches.

Eva Chen: exactly. sample trace shows many tiny matmuls (seq len buckets 8-64) causing kernel launch overheads and SM underutilization.

Raj Patel: suspect batching heuristic: we collapse requests with same model but not coalescing small-seq work. maybe batching window too tight.

Marta López: actionable ideas: 
1) bump batching window from 3ms -> 8ms for short-seq paths and re-measure.
2) enable intra-request fusion that merges consecutive small matmuls into a single batched GEMM when kv cache lookup is present.
3) add a small warm prefetch for KV entries to reduce attention_kv_cache_lookup spikes (prefetch threshold e.g., seq>32).

Eva Chen: also an easy experiment: force-run larger tile sizes in fused_gemm_attention_v2 (kernel config) to improve occupancy. patch attached below (very small):
```c
// patch snippet
if (seq_len <= 64) { grid.x = CEIL_DIV(batch*heads, 64); block.x = 128; }
else { grid.x = CEIL_DIV(batch*heads, 256); block.x = 256; }
```

Jin Park: note: that patch might increase per-kernel latency for huge seqs. need canary on dedicated cluster.

perf-bot: quick nvprof snippet to re-run targeted: 
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.free --format=csv
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,kernels --output out.nsys \ 
  --export=sqlite --capture-start=nvtx --capture-end=nvtx --sample=none \ 
  -- python -u run_inference.py --batch-size=1 --seqs=8,16,32 --warmup=10 --iters=200
nsys stats out.nsys --report=cuptiActivity --format=csv > out.kernels.csv
```

Raj Patel: can someone run the window/batch experiment and post results? I can do the canary for the kernel config if perf looks promising.

Marta López: running batch-window A/B now on infra-qa-3 (will post metrics). ETA ~45m.

Eva Chen: adding checklist:
- [ ] run A/B with window=3ms vs 8ms
- [ ] collect nsys and out.kernels.csv
- [ ] capture SM utilization and occupancy maps (nvprof/Perfetto)
- [ ] run canary for kernel tile-size patch on dedicated staging

Jin Park: small FYI: observed memcpy_HtoD spikes align with prefetch worker activity. if we spike prefetch parallelism that could starve GEMM. throttle prefetch threads if needed.

Marta López: posted interim numbers: 8ms window reduced number of fused_gemm_attention_v2 launches by ~43% and improved 99p tail by ~18% on qa. GPU SM util improved from 28% -> 46%.

Eva Chen: sweet. canary next. Raj, want me to hand off the kernel patch and perf artifacts?

Raj Patel: please do. I'll coordinate staging canary and keep an eye on regressions.

perf-bot: linked artifacts: s3://redwood/profiles/1905/kv-warm-sync.out.nsys, s3://redwood/profiles/1905/out.kernels.csv, perfetto://trace/1905/kv-warm.html

Marta López: tl;dr: root cause = many small matmuls from short-seq buckets + aggressive prefetch parallelism. fixes that helped: longer batching window + throttle prefetch + kernel-tile tweak as canary.

Eva Chen: thanks team. we'll iterate on fusion path too. :rocket:
